issues.issue: Automatic broadening by a state filing cannot easily be squared with Condition G, Change of Terms, which says the terms will not be waived, changed or modified except by written endorsement issued by the insurer.

The clause operates by reference to loss payees "shown on the SCHEDULE OF MORTGAGE HOLDERS OR LOSS PAYEES, Form RM1102," a form that does not appear on the POLICY INDEX (Form RM0003) or in the policy, so its subject matter is missing.
The paragraph is printed with stray numbering ("1. 5. 6.") before its single sentence, obscuring what falls within it.
It pays mortgage holders shown on Form RM1102, a schedule not listed on the POLICY INDEX and not attached, leaving the clause without any identified beneficiary.

"No person or organization having custody of your covered property will benefit from this policy" is drafted so broadly that its effect on bailees who are themselves additional named insureds, or on the Duty to Defend extension, is unclear.

The non-reduction rule is carved back for coverages "written with an annual aggregate limit," which requires reading it against the aggregate sublimits in the Pollution Cleanup extension and the Earth Movement and Flood endorsements to know what survives a loss.

The pure excess rule in Q.1 sits against Q.2, which contemplates proportionate contribution, and against Q.3-Q.4, which permit other insurance without reduction; how a concurrently insured loss is shared is not settled by any one of them.

The statement that other insurance "will not reduce any limit or sublimit" is difficult to square with Q.1, under which the existence of other insurance postpones this policy's obligation entirely until that insurance is exhausted.

The insurer's option to repair or replace must be exercised "within a reasonable period of time" and notified within sixty days of proof of loss, and the consequence of missing either period is not stated.
The two measures of a pair-or-set loss are joined by "or" with no indication of who chooses or which governs when they differ.
The payment obligation is conditioned on a list reading "1. ...; 2. ..., or 3. ...", so it is unclear whether all three conditions must be met or only the first plus one of the others.

The requirement that loss occur "during the policy period" must be read with the definition of period of restoration, which says expiration does not terminate it, and with the Transit definition, which continues coverage after expiry or cancellation.

The allocation sentence — recovery "in the proportion that your deductible and any provable uninsured loss bears to the total loss less your proportion of fees and expenses" — is syntactically tangled and yields no single arithmetic result.

"Within two (2) years ... or the shortest time permitted by law, whichever is greater" is internally confused: pairing the *shortest* period permitted by law with a "whichever is greater" test makes the applicable limitation period genuinely uncertain.

The KANSAS CHANGES endorsement (Form RM1815) deletes and replaces this condition with a five-year period running from the date the physical damage occurred, so the policy contains two different suit limitations.
"A dangerous condition relating to an object" permits immediate unilateral suspension of coverage without any defined standard for what is dangerous.
"Protective safeguards include, but are not limited to" a list of five systems, so the insured cannot tell what else it must maintain in complete working order to preserve coverage.

The second sanction ("Value the loss or damage ...") appears without its sub-letter, so it is unclear whether the valuation rule is an independent consequence or part of the preceding list of non-covered perils.
"Immediate written notice of the loss" fixes no period and is a condition on which several extensions expressly depend; what delay forfeits coverage is left entirely to argument.
The duties are printed with orphaned sub-letters ("a. b.") ahead of three separate obligations, and "as often as may reasonably be required" supplies no limit on repeated examinations under oath.

The ninety-day sworn proof of loss requirement interacts with Condition T, which makes payment due thirty days after an accepted proof, and with the suit limitation; whether a late proof forfeits the claim is not addressed.
"A sudden, fortuitous event" is undefined, and the carve-outs for "any other gradually developing condition" and conditions correctable by maintenance leave the boundary of an "accident" open.
"Replacement cost less deduction for depreciation" does not say whether depreciation may be taken on labour as well as materials, a recurring point of dispute.
"Less all charges and expenses which do not necessarily continue" is the operative deduction and turns on a judgment about necessity that the definition does not further specify.

The definition limits covered locations to those "shown on the Schedule," but the Declarations Schedule itself identifies covered locations only as those "per Statement of Values on file with us," a document outside the policy; which controls whether a given building is insured is genuinely contestable.
The definition is circular: a "covered loss" requires a "peril insured against," which is itself defined as a cause of loss "for which this policy provides coverage."

It confines covered loss to property "at a covered location," while Form RM1001 A. and B. insure property within 1,000 feet of a covered location and several extensions insure property in transit or away from any covered location.
"Covered property means property insured by this policy" is wholly circular and does no defining work, yet the term is the trigger for the insuring agreement and most exclusions.
